newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ING LAUNCHES ASSET MANAGEMENT SERVICES IN BRAZIL.
newsitem.headline: ING LAUNCHES ASSET MANAGEMENT SERVICES IN BRAZIL.

text.p: Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV said it has formed a company to provide asset management services in Brazil, joining an increasing team of foreign financial institutions that have recently entered the asset management business in the country.
ING Investment Management Brazil will focus on corporate clients, institutional investors and, in a further stage, high-income individuals, said Ricardo Leonardos, who was hired to build the firm.

Leonardos said the company will be under the ING Investment Management Americas region, one of the three divisions of the ING's asset management area. ING group, he said, concentrates on four main areas around the world: insurance, corporate, investment banking and asset management.
The new company will begin offering services to clients from ING Barings bank in Brazil, said Leonardos, who is currently involved in building the firm's staff of roughly 20 to 25 people.
"There is already a demand from ING corporate clients in Brazil for investment services," Leonardos said, adding that the company aims to administer about $2.0 billion in the next two or three years.

Leonardos said competition in the asset and investment services business in Brazil is growing, but he sees room for new players due to the huge growth potential of the country's fund industry and increased domestic savings.
Brazilian fund assets currently total about $200 billion, of which $77.1 billion are pension fund assets.
"The market will grow, particularly the pension industry," he said.
Most pension funds still administer their assets themselves, but several are already looking for independent managers.
He said the investment fund sector also is poised for growth as investors increasingly seek more sophisticated investments that provide higher returns.

ING is the latest to invest in the business in Brazil. Recently, U.S.-based Alliance Capital Management LP announced an equally-owned joint-venture with Brazilian private bank BCN to offer asset and investment services.

Prudential Securities, the fourth largest U.S. brokerage house, and Fidelity Investments, the world's largest mutual fund manager, opened their own offices in the country to also provide such services.
